citation: P. D. Maker, R. W. Terhune, M. Nisenoff, C. M. Savage, "Effects of dispersion and focusing on the production of optical harmonics", Phys. Rev. Lett. 8(1), 21-22 (1962)
readMethod: The request called this a 'Bjorkholm-type' paper; the PDF in docs/papers/ is the Maker et al. letter of 1962 (the Maker fringes), which is what was replicated. Read through macOS PDFKit: the 2 text pages (3-page PDF, third page blank) have a usable text layer except the equation and figure labels, so every number below was checked on a page image at 1.8x. The PDF and its figures are not in the repository.
topic: chi(2): dispersion-limited SHG in quartz (Maker fringes), phase matching in KDP, focused beams

referenceNumbers.where: p. 21, Fig. 1 (label 'dt theory = 13.9 um') and text

referenceNumbers.value: 300-fold increase of blue intensity at the matched orientation
referenceNumbers.status: read; no baseline stated, not a hard check

referenceNumbers.value: red photons per blue photon: quartz collimated 5e12, focused 6e10; KDP collimated at (theta0, phi0) 3e9, focused 1e6
3000 in KDP = 100 (beam diameter reduction) x 30 (mixing of diverging rays); one-inch focal-length lens
with a focused beam the blue is radiated only into the part of the cone with theta >= theta0

assumptions: The laser is a ruby laser (p. 21): 694.3 nm is assumed (the text gives no wavelength).

Which polarisation geometry makes the quartz harmonic is not clear from the text (it says the red is polarised parallel to the z axis while the plate is rotated about z). The ordinary-wave interaction (o o -> o, d11) is simulated: its fringe spacing, 13.7 um, is the one that matches 13.9 um; the extraordinary combination gives 13.25 um.
Quartz indices: Ghosh (1999), the same as the engine's Quartz material (the indices the 1961 authors used are not given). d_eff is set to a nominal 0.3 pm/V; only shapes are compared.
The plate is modelled as a plane-parallel slab at normal incidence with path length d / cos(theta_r); Fresnel factors at the tilted faces are not in the engine.
KDP data: the engine's built-in KDP (Zernike 1964); a 5 ps pulse stands in for the nanosecond-scale ruby pulse (quasi-cw).
Beam sizes of the focused and collimated beams are not given: collimated w0 = 300 um and focused w0 = 20 um are assumptions. The paper's photon ratios are laser-dependent and are not compared.
